s: Under the Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026, for up to how long may unmet targets be carried forward?
x: The 2026 amendment allows unmet targets to be carried forward for up to three years, not five.

s: Microbeads are prohibited under the Plastic Waste Management Rules in which products?
x: The PWM Rules ban microbeads in cosmetics; separately, an FSSAI study found microplastics in all tested sugar and salt samples.

s: Which of the following pairs (resin code – plastic) is correctly matched?
x: Resin code 1 is PET, 2 is HDPE, 3 is PVC and 5 is PP.

s: What is the minimum thickness of plastic carry bags in India from 31 December 2022?
x: Thickness rose from 40 (2011) to 50 (2016), 75 (30 September 2021) and 120 microns (31 December 2022).

s: On which date did India's ban on identified single-use plastic items come into force?
x: The SUP ban took effect on 1 July 2022; the EPR Guidelines on plastic packaging also became effective in July 2022.

s: Under the Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2024, from which body do makers of biodegradable plastics need certification?
o: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
x: The 2024 amendment defined biodegradable plastics and required CPCB certification for their makers.

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the identified single-use plastic items listed for prohibition?
o: Plastic sticks used in ear buds
x: Plastic ear-bud sticks, plastic flags and thermocol for decoration are included in the listed SUP items. HDPE milk bottles are not included in that list.

s: Which authorities are primarily responsible for enforcing the identified single-use plastic ban?
o: Only the Ministry of Jal Shakti
SPCBs/PCCs and local bodies, supported by national and state task forces
Only the National Disaster Management Authority
Only municipal corporations in metropolitan cities
x: Enforcement involves State Pollution Control Boards or Pollution Control Committees and local bodies, along with a National Level Taskforce and State Special Task Forces.

s: The identified single-use plastic ban covers approximately what proportion of total plastic waste?
x: The ban covers only about 11% of total plastic waste.

s: Under the plastic-packaging EPR framework, what is the full form of 'PIBOs'?
x: EPR applies to Producers, Importers and Brand Owners (PIBOs) for plastic packaging not covered by the SUP ban.

s: Under the plastic-packaging EPR framework, how does the recycled-content target for rigid plastics rise from 2025-26?
x: Rigid plastics go from 30% to 60%; flexible single-layer from 10% to 20%; multi-layered from 5% to 10%.

s: What do China's National Sword Policy of 2018 and Thailand's 2025 measure mainly restrict?
o: Domestic manufacture of all plastic products
x: China's National Sword Policy and Thailand's 2025 measure restrict imports of plastic waste.

s: UNEA-5.2, held in Nairobi in March 2022, adopted which resolution that led to the establishment of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC)?
x: The UNEA-5.2 resolution titled “End Plastic Pollution” established the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee.

s: Bisphenol A (BPA) is particularly associated with which resin-code category?
x: Resin code 7 ('others') includes polycarbonate, which releases bisphenol A (BPA), an endocrine disruptor. PET (1), PVC (3) and PP (5) are not the BPA-linked category.

s: Which standard must compostable plastics meet?
x: Compostable plastics must meet the IS/ISO 17088 standard.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the INC-5.2 plastics treaty meeting?
o: It was held in Geneva in August 2025
It ended with adoption of a final treaty text
Production caps and finance were major sticking points
x: INC-5.2 ended without agreement because of disputes over production caps, chemicals of concern and finance; no treaty text was adopted.

s: What are nurdles?
o: Secondary microplastics formed only by tyre wear
Primary microplastic pellets generally measuring 1–5 mm
Biodegradable plastic fibres used in clothing
x: Nurdles are primary microplastic pellets, generally 1–5 mm in size.

s: Up to what size are plastic particles generally called microplastics?
x: Microplastics are particles up to 5 mm (APPSC-GS 2023). 'Up to 5 micrometres only' is far too narrow, while 5-50 cm and above 5 mm describe larger debris.

s: Which was the first country to ban thin plastic bags, in 2002?
x: Bangladesh banned thin plastic bags in 2002; New Zealand's supermarket produce-bag ban came in July 2023.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: LDPE/HDPE — carry bags and milk bottles
x: Synthetic rubber is associated with tyres, not drinking-water bottles. LDPE/HDPE, synthetic polymers and cellulose acetate have the associations shown in the other options.

s: Under the PWM Amendment Rules, 2021, what was the minimum carry-bag thickness from 30 September 2021?
x: 75 microns applied from 30 September 2021 and 120 microns from 31 December 2022.

s: What carry-bag thickness did the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 set?
x: The 2016 Rules set 50 microns; the 2011 Rules had 40 microns.

s: Plastic roads were promoted under which rules?
x: The PWM Rules 2016 brought the 50-micron limit, a PWM fee and promoted plastic roads.

s: How many single-use plastic items were banned from 1 July 2022?
x: 19 identified single-use plastic items were banned from 1 July 2022; the ban covers only about 11% of plastic waste.

s: On whose portal do recyclers generate EPR certificates under the plastic-packaging framework?
x: On the CPCB EPR portal, recyclers generate tradable EPR certificates.

s: In July 2023, which country banned thin produce bags in supermarkets?
x: New Zealand banned thin produce bags in July 2023; Bangladesh was first to ban thin bags (2002).

s: Resin code 3 denotes which plastic?
x: Code 1 PET, 2 HDPE, 3 PVC, 4 LDPE, 5 PP, 6 PS, 7 others incl. polycarbonate.

s: Which body's study found microplastics in all tested samples of sugar and salt?
x: A study by FSSAI found microplastics in all the sugar and salt samples it tested.

s: What minimum thickness of plastic carry bags was set by the Plastic Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011?
x: The 2011 Rules set 40 microns; it rose to 50 (2016), 75 (2021) and 120 microns (2022).

s: Who was elected the new chair of the plastics treaty negotiating committee at INC-5.3 in Geneva in February 2026?
x: INC-5.3 (Geneva, February 2026) was organisational and elected Julio Cordano as the new chair.

s: Under GOBARdhan, launched in 2018 under SBM-Grameen, cattle dung, agricultural waste and solid waste are converted into what?
x: GOBARdhan promotes conversion of cattle dung, agricultural waste and solid waste into biogas and bio-slurry, supported by a unified portal.

s: Indore, recognised as India's model zero-waste and landfill-free city, is in which State?
x: Indore in Madhya Pradesh is the model zero-waste, landfill-free city of India.

s: What is the main target of SBM-Urban 2.0, implemented during 2021-26?
x: SBM-Urban 2.0, covering 2021-26, targets garbage-free cities.

s: Which scheme aims to formalise informal sanitation and waste workers?
x: NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem) aims to bring informal sanitation workers, and since 2024 waste pickers, into the formal system with safety and dignity. PM SVANidhi, PM-DAKSH and Stand-Up India are other schemes.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its principal focus?
o: Total Sanitation Campaign — only construction of subsidised rural latrines
Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan — introduction of sanitation for the first time in India
Central Rural Sanitation Programme — award for ODF gram panchayats
Integrated Low Cost Sanitation — conversion of dry latrines to pour-flush latrines and liberation of manual scavengers
x: The Integrated Low Cost Sanitation programme focused on converting dry latrines into pour-flush latrines and freeing manual scavengers. The other options assign incorrect descriptions.

s: Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan, introduced in 2012, was the renamed form of which programme?
x: Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan was the renamed Total Sanitation Campaign and followed a saturation approach.

s: When was Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban launched?
x: SBM-Urban was launched on 2 October 2014.

s: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, which implements Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen, is under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: SBM-Grameen is run by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. The ministry was renamed in June 2019.

s: Phase I of SBM-Grameen aimed to construct over how many toilets by 2019-20?
x: Phase I aimed at over 10 crore toilets and ODF villages; rural sanitation coverage rose from 39% (2014) to 100% (2019).

s: Which is the highest of the three progressive levels of ODF Plus villages under SBM-Grameen?
x: ODF Plus levels run Aspiring, then Rising, then Model, which is the highest.

s: What is the incentive given under SBM-Grameen for the construction of an Individual Household Latrine (IHHL)?
x: The IHHL incentive under SBM-G is ₹12,000. ₹6,000, ₹10,000 and ₹15,000 are not the stated amount; separately, greywater support is ₹280/capita (villages up to 5,000) and ₹660/capita (above 5,000).

s: When was Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0 launched?
x: SBM-U 2.0 was launched on 1 October 2021, runs till 2026, has an outlay of about ₹1.41 lakh crore and is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme covering all statutory towns.

s: The Garbage Free City star-rating system provides which of the following ratings?
x: The Garbage Free City certification uses 1-star, 3-star, 5-star and 7-star ratings for waste management.

s: Which body conducts Swachh Survekshan, run by MoHUA under SBM-Urban?
x: Swachh Survekshan, begun in 2016 under MoHUA, is conducted by the Quality Council of India.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the cleanest-city result for the 2023 edition of Swachh Survekshan in the 10 lakh-plus category?
x: Indore and Surat jointly occupied the cleanest-city position in the 2023 edition for cities with more than 10 lakh population.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the SATAT–GOBARdhan linkage?
o: It establishes 500 new MRFs exclusively for e-waste.
It provides 500 MW from existing WtE plants only.
It targets 500 new waste-to-wealth CBG plants.
x: The SATAT and GOBARdhan linkage targets 500 new waste-to-wealth compressed biogas plants.

s: Which one of the following statements about Swachhata Hi Seva is correct?
o: It is an award given to ODF gram panchayats.
It is a plastic-import restriction introduced in 2018.
It is a ten-year rural sanitation strategy beginning in 2019.
It is a fortnight-long shramdaan campaign conducted every year since 2017.
x: Swachhata Hi Seva has been observed as a fortnight shramdaan campaign every year since 2017.

s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: ODF+ — safe management of faecal sludge
ODF++ — toilets that are functional, clean and maintained
Water+ — used water treated before discharge
Garbage Free City — certification based only on toilet construction
x: Water+ certification signifies that used water is treated before discharge. ODF+ concerns functional, clean and maintained toilets, while ODF++ adds safe faecal-sludge management.

s: In which year was the Total Sanitation Campaign launched?
x: TSC began in 1999; CRSP 1986; Nirmal Gram Puraskar 2003; Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan 2012.

s: What was Nirmal Gram Puraskar, introduced in 2003?
x: Nirmal Gram Puraskar (2003) was an award for ODF panchayats.

s: On which date is Swachh Bharat Diwas observed?
x: Swachh Bharat Diwas is 2 October; Swachhata Hi Seva is a fortnight of shramdaan held since 2017.

s: Under SBM-Urban 2.0, 'ODF++' certification adds which requirement to ODF+?
x: ODF++ adds safe faecal-sludge management; Water+ adds treatment of used water before discharge.

s: What is the approximate outlay of SBM-Urban 2.0 (2021-26)?
x: SBM-U 2.0 has an outlay of ₹1.41 lakh crore and covers all statutory towns.

s: Under SBM-Grameen, what is the greywater management assistance for villages with a population up to 5,000?
x: Greywater: ₹280/capita up to 5,000 population and ₹660/capita above 5,000.

s: In Swachh Survekshan 2024-25, which city was the cleanest big city?
x: Ahmedabad was the cleanest big city; Indore, Surat and Navi Mumbai were in the Super Swachh League.

s: Which edition of Swachh Survekshan had the theme 'Waste to Wealth'?
x: Swachh Survekshan 2023, the eighth edition, had the theme 'Waste to Wealth'.

s: Which Ministry runs the Swachh Survekshan cleanliness survey?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: Swachh Survekshan is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA); the Quality Council of India conducts it.

s: In which year was the Swachh Survekshan first held?
x: Swachh Survekshan has been held since 2016; Swachh Survekshan Grameen began in 2018.

s: Which city was ranked the cleanest city of India in Swachh Survekshan 2017?
x: In Swachh Survekshan 2017 Indore was the cleanest city and Gonda (UP) the dirtiest.

s: Which cities were placed in the Super Swachh League of Swachh Survekshan 2024-25?
x: Swachh Survekshan 2024-25 put Indore, Surat and Navi Mumbai in the Super Swachh League; Ahmedabad was the cleanest big city.

s: In which year was the Integrated Low Cost Sanitation (ILCS) scheme, which converted dry latrines into pour-flush latrines, launched?
x: ILCS began in 1980-81; the Central Rural Sanitation Programme came in 1986 and the Total Sanitation Campaign in 1999.

s: Which Ministry launched the ten-year Rural Sanitation Strategy (2019-2029) in September 2019?
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
x: The Ministry of Jal Shakti launched the Rural Sanitation Strategy in September 2019; it was prepared by DDWS.

s: In Swachh Survekshan 2024-25, Indore was named the cleanest city for which time?
x: Swachh Survekshan 2024-25 marked Indore's eighth time as the cleanest city.

s: Which city was ranked the dirtiest city in Swachh Survekshan 2017?
x: In Swachh Survekshan 2017, Indore was the cleanest and Gonda (UP) the dirtiest city.

s: From which year has Swachh Survekshan Grameen been conducted?
x: Swachh Survekshan began in 2016; its rural version, SS Grameen, began in 2018.

s: In which year was the Central Rural Sanitation Programme launched?
x: The Central Rural Sanitation Programme for rural latrines began in 1986.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Indore is a model zero-waste, landfill-free city.
2. The Indore method of composting is an anaerobic pit method.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Indore is the model zero-waste city; the Indore method is aerobic composting, while the Bangalore method is the anaerobic pit.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about sanitary landfills?
o: Waste is compacted in cells and covered with earth daily.
The method relies mainly on containment rather than treatment.
Liners and leachate-collection systems are used.
They are intended for all biodegradable waste without segregation.
x: Sanitary landfills are not meant for all biodegradable waste without segregation; the other features are correct.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about waste-to-energy technologies?
o: Incineration burns waste in the absence of oxygen.
Incineration can reduce waste volume by about 90 per cent.
Incineration may generate ash and emissions.
Biomethanation converts wet organic waste into biogas through microbial action.
x: Incineration burns waste in oxygen (and may produce steam for power); it does not work in the absence of oxygen.

s: In which of the following is Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) mainly used as an alternative fuel?
o: Cement kilns and thermal power plants
x: RDF, made by shredding and dehydrating high-calorific MSW, is used in cement kilns and thermal power plants.

s: Which of the following describes the Indore method of composting?
o: Anaerobic pits with alternate layers of solid waste and night soil
Aerobic composting with the waste turned at intervals
x: The Indore method is aerobic composting with turning at intervals; anaerobic pits with layers of MSW and night soil are the Bangalore method.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes incineration from pyrolysis?
o: Incineration heats waste in the absence of oxygen, whereas pyrolysis uses excess oxygen
Incineration is controlled high-temperature burning, whereas pyrolysis heats waste without oxygen
Both methods are biological processes using earthworms
Both methods are restricted to inert waste in sanitary landfills
x: Incineration is controlled high-temperature combustion, while pyrolysis is thermal treatment in the absence of oxygen.

s: Which of the following pairs (waste – preferred method) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Biomedical waste – Incineration at a common treatment facility
x: High-calorific dry waste is used as RDF or co-processed in cement kilns, not landfilled.

s: With the help of which organisms is vermicompost produced?
x: Vermicompost is made by earthworms, which makes vermicomposting a biological method of composting.

s: Which alternative method is associated with oil spills and oily sludge?
x: Oilzapper, a mix of bacteria, cleans up oil spills and oily sludge. A microbial fuel cell treats wastewater, and EPR is a producer duty.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Bioremediation – Using naturally occurring organisms to remove pollutants
UV purification – Thermal breakdown of waste without oxygen
Pyrolysis – Thermal breakdown of waste without oxygen to recover energy
x: UV purification kills microorganisms in drinking water; thermal breakdown without oxygen is pyrolysis.

s: Hydrogen is regarded as a clean fuel because hydrogen fuel cells emit only which of the following?
x: Hydrogen fuel cells emit only water vapour, which is why hydrogen is considered a clean fuel.

s: Which method of solid-waste disposal is described as not viable in urban India?
x: Composting, incineration and landfilling are all used in urban India; only uncontrolled dumping is described as not viable.

s: Which of the following is compost?
o: Disposal of solid waste in a designated land area
Decomposed organic waste that becomes nutrient-rich material
x: Compost is organic waste that has broken down into nutrient-rich material. The other options describe landfill, recycling and incineration.

s: By about how much does incineration reduce the volume of waste?
x: Controlled burning in oxygen at high heat cuts waste volume by about 90%.

s: What does plasma gasification produce using electricity and high heat without combustion?
x: Plasma gasification produces syngas and can dispose of all organic wastes.

s: Which method is best for the disposal of broken glass?
x: In the APPSC-G2 2023 match, broken glass goes to landfilling; organic waste to composting, e-waste to recycling.

s: The Bangalore method of composting takes about how long?
x: The Bangalore method uses anaerobic pits with alternate layers of MSW and night soil for 4–6 months.

s: From which of the following is Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) made?
x: RDF is shredded, dehydrated high-calorific MSW used as fuel in cement kilns and thermal plants.

s: Which of the following is a waste-to-energy process?
x: Pyrolysis (like plasma gasification) is a waste-to-energy process; compost and vermicompost turn waste into manure, not energy.

s: Which method of waste disposal is low in cost but has a long-term environmental impact?
x: Landfilling is cheap, but it harms the environment over a long time.

s: Which method of waste disposal conserves resources but needs infrastructure?
x: Recycling saves resources but needs collection and processing infrastructure.

s: Which gas can be produced by the anaerobic decomposition of biodegradable waste?
x: Anaerobic decomposition produces methane or biogas, while aerobic decomposition produces compost.

s: Solid waste includes discarded material in solid, liquid, semi-solid and which other form?
x: The definition covers discarded or abandoned materials that are solid, liquid, semi-solid or containerised gaseous.

s: Which of the following best defines e-waste in the context of the ITU definition?
o: Only hazardous electronic equipment exported across borders
Only discarded computers sent for recycling
All household waste containing any metal component
Discarded electrical and electronic equipment and parts not meant for reuse
x: E-waste consists of discarded electrical and electronic equipment and parts that are not intended for reuse.

s: According to the stated healthcare-waste composition, approximately what proportion of healthcare waste is general non-hazardous waste?
x: Approximately 85% of healthcare waste is general non-hazardous waste, while about 15% is hazardous, including infectious, chemical and radioactive waste.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four classic characteristics used to identify hazardous waste?
x: The four classic characteristics are ignitability, corrosivity, reactivity and toxicity. Biodegradability is not one of these four classic criteria.

s: Which of the following is an example of household hazardous waste?
x: Paints and batteries are household hazardous waste; the others are biodegradable or non-hazardous household wastes.

s: Biomedical waste arises from the diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of whom?
x: Biomedical waste arises from the diagnosis, treatment or immunisation of humans or animals and includes blood, sharps, cultures and expired medicines.

s: Which of the following is an impact of non-biodegradable plastics?
x: Non-biodegradable plastics persist, pollute, break into microplastics, create landfill problems and harm wildlife.

s:
Assertion (A): Biodegradable polymers are eco-friendly.
Reason (R): They are degraded by microorganisms.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: microbes break biodegradable polymers down, so they do not pile up in the environment.

s: Paddy husk and cattle dung belong to which category of solid waste?
x: Agricultural waste covers crop residues, paddy husk and cattle dung; it is biodegradable and dung becomes biogas under GOBARdhan.

s: What does construction and demolition waste mostly consist of?
o: Inert material such as concrete, bricks and debris
x: C&D waste is mostly inert – concrete, bricks, dirt, rocks and debris.

s: How are natural rubber and wool classified?
x: Wool (keratin fibre) and natural rubber are biodegradable; synthetic rubber is not.

s: Polythene is a polymer of which of the following?
x: Polythene is a polymer of ethylene (C2H4); PVC is made from vinyl chloride.

s: Which of the following polymers is biodegradable?
x: PHBV, Nylon-2-Nylon-6, PLA and PGA are biodegradable polymers; PVC, Teflon and polystyrene are not.

s: Of total healthcare waste, about what share is hazardous (infectious, chemical or radioactive), as per WHO?
x: About 85% of healthcare waste is general non-hazardous and about 15% hazardous.

s: Expanded 5R versions of the waste hierarchy may add which two Rs?
x: Expanded 5R versions may add Refuse and Repurpose (or, in some versions, Recover).

s: Which one of the following best illustrates the contribution of biomining of legacy waste to a circular economy?
o: It permanently stores all waste without recovery.
It increases the generation of mixed municipal waste.
It recovers useful materials from old waste dumps for productive reuse.
It replaces source reduction with open dumping.
x: Biomining of legacy waste supports the circular economy by recovering materials from old waste accumulations for reuse or further processing.

s: What is the name given to old municipal solid waste piled in dumpsites for years, emitting methane and polluting groundwater?
x: That is legacy waste; biomining excavates it and separates it into recyclables, RDF, bio-soil and inert fill.

s: Which of the following pairs (industrial waste – source) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Fly ash – Coal-based thermal power plants
x: Red mud comes from alumina refining; phosphogypsum comes from phosphoric acid or phosphatic fertiliser plants.

s: Within what distance of thermal plants does the Fly Ash Utilisation Notification require the use of fly ash in bricks, cement and roads?
x: The notification applies within 300 km of thermal plants; fly ash can make bricks and partly replace Portland cement.

s: Surat is known for a road built using which industrial waste?
x: Surat has a steel-slag road; steel slag is used as road base, to improve agricultural soil and in cement production.

s: Under which mission is every city intended to have a permanent RRR Centre?
o: The Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016
x: Every city has a permanent RRR Centre under SBM-U 2.0. RRR is expanded in the cited context as Reduce, Reuse and Recover.

s: Which statement regarding the waste hierarchy is correct?
o: Reduction at source is the top priority in the 3R approach.
Regain replaces Reduce in the standard 3R formulation.
Recycling means using an item again in its original form.
Reuse means converting waste into a different usable material.
x: Reduction at source is the top priority. Reuse means using an item again in its existing form, while recycling converts waste into other usable materials.

s: Which of the following statements about solid waste management is incorrect?
o: It involves the collection of waste.
It involves the processing of waste.
Landfilling is the most preferred option in the waste hierarchy.
It involves the final disposal of waste.
x: Option C is incorrect: in the waste hierarchy landfilling is the least preferred option, after reduction, reuse, recycling and recovery. Solid waste management does involve collection, processing and disposal.

s: In the waste hierarchy, what is using an item again in the same form called?
x: Reuse means using the item again in the same form; recycling converts waste into other usable materials.

s: Phosphogypsum, used as a gypsum substitute and soil conditioner, comes from which of the following?
o: Phosphoric acid and phosphatic fertiliser plants
x: Phosphogypsum is a by-product of phosphoric acid / phosphatic fertiliser plants.

s: Chromium sludge is a hazardous waste mainly from which industry?
x: Chromium sludge comes from tanneries.

s: Fly ash can partly replace which material, as noted in UPSC 2015?
x: Fly ash partly replaces Portland cement and is used in bricks, cement and roads within 300 km of thermal plants.

s:
Consider the following statements about steel slag:
1. It can be used as road base.
2. It can be used in agricultural soil.
3. It can be used in cement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Steel slag can be used for road base, agricultural soil and cement – all three (UPSC 2020).

s: Red mud is a waste of which industry?
x: Red mud comes from alumina refining; steel slag from steel plants, phosphogypsum from phosphoric acid plants.

s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, waste was required to be segregated into which three streams?
o: Biodegradable, dry and domestic hazardous waste
x: The three streams under the 2016 Rules were biodegradable waste, dry waste and domestic hazardous waste.

s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, every waste generator is required to segregate waste into which of the following four streams?
o: Wet, dry, sanitary and special care
x: The four streams are wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste, the last category covering domestic hazardous waste.

s: Which one of the following changes has been reported in the composition of rural waste?
o: A shift from municipal waste towards only industrial hazardous waste
A shift from biodegradable waste towards plastic, sanitary and other non-biodegradable waste
A complete disappearance of sanitary waste from rural areas
A shift from plastic waste towards exclusively biodegradable waste
x: Rural waste is shifting from predominantly biodegradable waste towards plastic, sanitary and other non-biodegradable waste.

s: In the composition of Indian municipal solid waste, which component accounts for approximately 55–60 per cent?
x: Biodegradable material constitutes approximately 55–60 per cent of Indian municipal solid waste.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about solid waste in India?
o: Urban areas account for only about 20% of all waste generated
About 60% of waste comes from urban areas
x: About 60% of India's waste comes from urban areas, not 20%; SBM-U processing rose from 16% (2014) to 82% (2026).

s: Where was India's first major nurdle landing reported?
o: Kerala, from the MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck
West Bengal, from a fishing vessel
x: The first major nurdle landing in India occurred in Kerala following the MSC Elsa 3 shipwreck. The nurdles included LDPE and HDPE.

s: India generates about how much municipal solid waste a year?
x: India generates over 62 million tonnes of MSW a year, about 60% of it urban.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Maharashtra produces the highest solid waste among Indian States.
2. Delhi generates the largest solid waste per person among India's mega cities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Maharashtra is the highest solid-waste State and Delhi is the mega city with the most solid waste per person.

s: Which of the following was a provision of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016?
o: Unrestricted disposal of untreated waste in landfills
Exemption of brand owners from waste responsibility
Extended producer responsibility for producers and brand owners
x: The 2016 Rules provided for user fees, spot fines and EPR for producers and brand owners, and prohibited untreated waste in landfills.

s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, what must a Bulk Waste Generator do?
o: Send all its wet waste to a landfill
Hand over unsegregated waste to the Urban Local Body
Process wet waste on site or obtain an EBWGR certificate
Mix sanitary waste with dry recyclable waste
x: Bulk Waste Generators must process wet waste on site or obtain an EBWGR certificate under the 2026 Rules.

s: Environmental Compensation under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 follows which principle?
x: Environmental Compensation follows the polluter-pays principle, not the precautionary principle.

s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, used diapers and sanitary napkins were generally to be wrapped and placed in which stream?
x: Under the 2016 system, used diapers and sanitary napkins were generally wrapped and placed in the dry bin. The 2026 Rules provide a separate sanitary stream.

s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, paper, plastics and metals go into which bin?
x: Paper, plastics and metals go in the dry bin; wet waste covers food scraps, peels and garden waste.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold in its order of 18 August 2026 on responsibility for waste at the threshold?
o: Only Urban Local Bodies are responsible for such waste
Only sanitary workers are responsible for such waste
Responsibility begins only after waste reaches a landfill
Generators, and not only sanitary workers, are responsible for such waste
x: The Supreme Court held that generators, and not only sanitary workers, are responsible for waste at the threshold.

s: In the municipal solid-waste collection chain, which step comes immediately before the Material Recovery Facility (MRF)?
x: The chain runs door-to-door collection, segregated transport, transfer station, MRF, processing/recycling and residual landfill.

s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, used diapers and sanitary napkins go into which stream?
x: The 2026 Rules create a separate sanitary stream; under 2016 they were wrapped into the dry bin.

s: In the municipal waste collection chain, which step comes immediately after the Material Recovery Facility?
x: The chain is door-to-door, segregated transport, transfer station, MRF, processing/recycling, then residual landfill.

s: On which date did the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 come into effect?
x: The SWM Rules 2016 took effect from 8 April 2016 and extended beyond municipal areas.

s: On which date did the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 come into force?
x: The SWM Rules 2026 (under EPA 1986) are in force from 1 April 2026; 1 Oct 2025 was the draft proposal.

s: In February 2026, the Supreme Court held that a clean environment is part of which Article of the Constitution?
x: The Supreme Court treats the right to a clean environment as part of the right to life under Article 21.

s: Under which Act were the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 framed?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
x: The SWM Rules 2026 were notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and came into force on 1 April 2026.

s: Which of the following is an example of ‘invisible e-waste’ commonly discarded with regular waste?
o: Vapes, USB cables and LED accessories
Glass bottles, steel cans and paper cartons
Construction aggregates, fly ash and cement bags
Food scraps, garden leaves and crop residue
x: Vapes, USB cables and LED accessories are examples of ‘invisible e-waste’ that may be thrown into regular waste streams.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Landfill is associated with solid waste disposal.
EPR refers to the producer's end-of-life responsibility.
R2 refers to wastewater treatment and electricity generation.
x: Option C is incorrect: R2 is about responsible electronics recycling. Wastewater treatment with electricity is the microbial fuel cell.

s:
Consider the following statements about Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR):
1. EPR was first brought into Indian law by the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016.
2. Under EPR, a producer is responsible for the environmentally sound management of a product till the end of its life.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: EPR first came into Indian law through the E-waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2011, so statement 1 is wrong; statement 2 is the meaning of EPR.

s: Which organisations jointly publish the Global E-waste Monitor?
x: The Global E-waste Monitor is published by the International Telecommunication Union and the United Nations Institute for Training and Research.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about EPR under the E-waste Rules, 2022?
o: Producers may buy digital EPR certificates from unregistered recyclers.
Producers receive annual recycling targets based on earlier sales.
Producers register on the CPCB portal.
An EPR floor price is intended to protect formal recyclers.
x: Producers buy digital EPR certificates from registered recyclers, not unregistered ones.

s: Which of the following persons or entities may legally deal in e-waste under the E-waste (Management) Rules, 2022?
o: Only registered producers, manufacturers, refurbishers and recyclers
x: The Rules permit only registered producers, manufacturers, refurbishers and recyclers to deal in e-waste.

s: Which of the following is correctly arranged as the authorised e-waste recycling chain?
o: Producer → consumer → landfill → dismantler → recovered materials
Consumer → collection centre or producer take-back → authorised dismantler → authorised recycler → recovered materials
Consumer → informal hub → landfill → authorised recycler → producer take-back
Consumer → authorised recycler → collection centre → informal hub → recovered materials
x: The authorised chain begins with the consumer and collection or producer take-back, followed by dismantling, recycling and recovery of materials.

s: What is India's rank among the world's largest generators of e-waste, after China and the United States?
x: India is the third-largest e-waste generator, after China and the United States.

s: About how much e-waste did India generate in 2025?
x: India’s e-waste generation was reported as approximately 2.2 million tonnes in 2025. The 3.54 lakh tonnes figure refers to e-waste collected and processed in FY 2021.

s: Which of the following pairs (e-waste constituent – main harm) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Brominated flame retardants – Persistent nature and endocrine effects
Mercury – Brain and kidney damage; bioaccumulation in fish
Cadmium – Persistent nature and endocrine effects
x: Cadmium causes kidney and bone damage; persistence and endocrine effects describe brominated flame retardants (PBBs).

s: On which date did the E-waste (Management) Rules, 2022 come into force?
x: The Rules were notified in November 2022 and came into force on 1 April 2023; their 106 EEE items include solar PV waste.

s: The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 replaced the battery rules of which year?
x: The 2022 Rules replaced the 2001 rules and cover EV, portable, automotive and industrial batteries under EPR.

s: Which pair of places is correctly associated with informal e-waste recycling hubs?
x: Seelampur in Delhi and Moradabad are identified as informal e-waste recycling hubs.

s: Which one of the following is the most appropriate action for a citizen disposing of an old electronic device?
o: Burn it to recover copper and aluminium
Mix it with municipal solid waste after removing the battery
Sell or deposit it with an authorised recycler or collection centre after wiping data
Hand it over to any informal dismantler without data removal
x: Citizens should use authorised recyclers or collection centres and wipe personal data before handing over old electronics.

s: According to MeitY, approximately how much e-waste was collected and processed in India in FY 2021?
x: MeitY put e-waste collected and processed in FY 2021 at about 3.54 lakh tonnes (APPSC-GS 2021 key). 2.2 MT (2025) and 1.75 MT are generation figures, and 35.4 lakh tonnes is ten times the stated value.

s: How many EEE items are covered by the E-waste (Management) Rules, 2022?
x: The 2022 Rules cover 106 EEE items, including solar PV waste.

s: As per the Global E-waste Monitor 2024, about what share of e-waste in 2022 was formally recycled?
x: GEM 2024: 62 million tonnes generated in 2022, only 22.3% formally recycled.

s: How much global e-waste generation in 2022 did the Global E-waste Monitor 2024 report?
x: 62 Mt in 2022, projected to reach 82 Mt by 2030.

s: About what share of e-waste in India is processed informally?
x: About 78% of e-waste is processed informally, in hubs like Seelampur and Moradabad.

s: Which e-waste constituent mainly harms the kidney and bone?
x: Cadmium harms kidney and bone; mercury harms brain and kidney; PBBs have endocrine effects.

s: Which of the following wastes is covered under the E-waste (Management) Rules, 2022?
x: The E-waste (Management) Rules, 2022 cover 106 EEE items, including solar PV waste.

s: The Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016 replaced which earlier rules?
o: Municipal Solid Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2000
x: The Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016 replaced the Biomedical Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 1998, which had ten categories.

s: In hazardous-waste disposal, which option is treated as the last resort?
x: Landfill is the last resort; APPCB prefers co-processing as fuel in cement plants and waste exchange between industries.

s: Which of the following was issued by the CPCB in response to biomedical waste generated during the COVID-19 period?
o: Global E-waste Monitor and Basel Protocol
R2 electronics recycling code and plastic treaty guidelines
COVID19BWM tracking app and COVID-19 waste guidelines
x: The CPCB issued COVID-19 biomedical-waste guidelines in 2020 and introduced the COVID19BWM tracking app.

s: What is the main purpose of treating biomedical waste before disposal?
o: Increase the calorific value of hospital waste
Prevent the spread of infection and protect human health
Convert all biomedical waste into compost
Allow syringes to be reused safely
x: BMW is treated before disposal mainly to prevent infection spread and protect human health (APPSC-GS 2025) - killing pathogens, stopping syringe reuse and cutting volume and toxicity. Raising calorific value is not the aim, composting is not the route, and treatment is meant to stop syringe reuse, not enable it.

s: How many colour categories do the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016 use?
x: The 2016 Rules use four colour categories with barcoding and GPS tracking; ten categories belonged to the 1998 Rules.

s: Under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016, contaminated recyclable plastics such as IV sets and catheters go into which category?
x: Contaminated recyclable plastics go into Red; Yellow is for anatomical waste and expired medicines.

s: Under the BMW Rules, 2016, sharps such as needles and blades go into which category?
x: Sharps go into White (translucent); glassware into Blue; recyclable plastics into Red.

s: How is yellow-category biomedical waste such as anatomical waste treated?
o: Incineration, plasma pyrolysis or deep burial
x: Yellow waste goes for incineration, plasma pyrolysis or deep burial; Red goes for autoclave/microwave and shredding.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016:
1. They replaced the 1998 Rules.
2. They introduced barcoding and GPS tracking.
3. They have not been amended since 2016.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 2016 Rules replaced the 1998 Rules and use barcoding and GPS; they were amended in 2018 and 2019, so 3 is wrong.

s: Under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016, glassware and metallic implants go into which colour category?
x: Blue category holds glassware and metallic implants, treated by disinfection and recycling.

s: The Environment (Construction and Demolition Waste Management) Rules, 2025 introduced which framework for C&D waste?
x: MoEFCC notified an Extended Producer Responsibility framework for C&D waste under the 2025 Rules.

s: What is the main purpose of the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991?
o: Compensation only after criminal conviction of the polluter
No-fault insurance cover and immediate relief to victims of hazardous-substance accidents
Insurance exclusively for transport of municipal waste
Long-term subsidies to industries using fly ash
x: The Act provides no-fault insurance cover intended to give immediate relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous substances.

s: Mercury-added products such as fluorescent lamps are being phased out under which convention?
x: Mercury-added products are phased out under the Minamata Convention; Stockholm deals with persistent organic pollutants.

s: Under the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016, which is at the top of the waste-management hierarchy?
x: Prevention is at the top of the hierarchy; co-processing comes later, before safe disposal.

s: From which date did the Environment (Construction and Demolition) Waste Management Rules, 2025 take effect?
x: The 2025 C&D Rules took effect from 1 April 2026; 1 October 2025 was the date in the draft SWM Rules.

s: Which group of chemicals is often called 'forever chemicals'?
x: PFAS persist in the environment, occur in products such as food packaging and can accumulate in animal bodies.

s: In the context of transboundary movement of hazardous waste, what is the full form of PIC?
x: PIC means Prior Informed Consent, a control associated with the import and export of hazardous waste.

s: By which year is the phase-out of dental amalgam targeted under the Minamata Convention framework?
x: The Minamata Convention concerns mercury, and dental amalgam phase-out is targeted by 2034.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MSIHC Rules, 1989 — manufacture, storage and import of hazardous chemicals
CAEPPR Rules, 1996 — insurance compensation without fault
Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 — constitution of crisis groups
Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025 — regulation of fluorescent lamp manufacture
x: The MSIHC Rules, 1989 address the manufacture, storage and import of hazardous chemicals. CAEPPR concerns crisis groups, while the Public Liability Insurance Act provides no-fault relief.

s: What does the ITPGRFA deal with?
x: ITPGRFA covers plant genetic resources; Ramsar covers wetlands and Stockholm covers POPs.

s: Which of the following pairs (convention – subject) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Basel – Transboundary movement of hazardous wastes
x: The Rotterdam Convention covers Prior Informed Consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides in trade; mercury is covered by Minamata.

s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted in the aftermath of which event?
x: The EPA 1986 was enacted after the Bhopal gas tragedy (1984). The Stockholm Conference and Chernobyl are not the stated trigger, and Minamata gave its name to the 2013 mercury convention.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Bhopal disaster in December 1984 involved methyl isocyanate. The LG Polymers incident at Visakhapatnam in May 2020 involved styrene vapour.

s: Which Rio convention is associated with desertification?
x: The UNCCD covers desertification; the CBD covers biodiversity and the UNFCCC climate change.

s: Where was India's first C&D waste recycling plant set up?
x: The first C&D waste recycling plant is at Burari (Delhi); India generates about 12 million tonnes of C&D waste a year.

s: The EPR framework under the C&D Waste Management Rules, 2025 applies to producers with projects of at least what size?
x: EPR applies to producers with projects of 20,000 sq m or more; recycling targets go from 25% (2025-26) to 100% (2028-29).

s: Which gas leaked in the LG Polymers accident at Visakhapatnam in May 2020?
x: LG Polymers (May 2020) leaked styrene vapour; Bhopal (1984) involved methyl isocyanate.

s: Where is hazardous waste that must be landfilled disposed of?
x: Hazardous waste disposal uses secure landfills, and landfill is the last resort.

s: When did India ratify the Basel Convention?
x: India ratified Basel in June 1992; it acceded to Rotterdam in 2005.

s: What is the Rotterdam Convention concerned with?
o: Prior Informed Consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides in trade
x: Rotterdam (2004) is about Prior Informed Consent; Stockholm POPs; Minamata mercury; Ramsar wetlands.

s: About how much construction and demolition waste does India generate a year?
x: India generates about 12 million tonnes of C&D waste a year.

s: Under the Environment (C&D Waste Management) Rules, 2025, the recycling target rises from 25% in 2025-26 to what level by 2028-29?
x: The C&D Rules 2025 set recycling targets of 25% in 2025-26 rising to 100% by 2028-29.

s: PFAS and chlorpyrifos are listed under which international convention?
x: The Stockholm Convention on POPs now lists 34 chemicals, including PFAS and chlorpyrifos.

s: For what purpose is biomedical waste in Andhra Pradesh mainly sent to Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facilities?
o: Production of RDF for cement kilns only
x: Biomedical waste is sent to Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facilities for incineration. It is not intended for open dumping or untreated agricultural composting.

s: How many Municipal Corporations does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: AP's urban set-up has 17 Municipal Corporations, 113 municipalities and 7 cantonment boards.

s: As stated by the Chief Minister in February 2026, Andhra Pradesh inherited about how much legacy waste?
x: AP inherited about 108 lakh tonnes of legacy waste; Ongole is biomining its Guthikondavaripalem dump yard and supplying RDF to cement plants.

s: In Andhra Pradesh, the ban on single-use plastic applies to carry bags below what thickness?
x: Andhra Pradesh bans single-use plastic and carry bags below 120 microns, with enforcement involving the Revenue Department, Police and Pollution Control Board.

s: For what purpose did the Municipal Administration Department launch Operation Clean Sweep in May 2026?
o: Scientific solid-waste management in Tier-1 and Tier-2 corporations
Only coastal plastic clean-up in villages
x: Operation Clean Sweep (May–June 2026) is the Municipal Administration Department's sanitation drive for scientific solid-waste management in all 123 ULBs: clearing garbage black spots, cleaning roads and drains and promoting segregation.

s: Where are the two Common Hazardous Waste Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facilities (CHWTSDFs) of Andhra Pradesh located?
x: The two CHWTSDFs identified for Andhra Pradesh are located in Anakapalli and SPSR Nellore.

s: Which system is used by APEMC for tracking hazardous-waste movement in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Biometric tracking of every waste container
x: APEMC uses GPS tracking for monitoring hazardous-waste movement and management.

s: Which agency functions as the state agency running urban sanitation under SBM-U 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education
x: Swachha Andhra Corporation, or SAC, is the state agency running urban sanitation under SBM-U 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh.

s: The Re Sustainability MoU in Andhra Pradesh for e-waste collection and material recovery facilities covers how many ULBs?
x: The Re Sustainability MoU covers all 123 ULBs; the 30-ULB figure relates to the ITC MoU.

s: By what name was the Clean Andhra Pradesh (CLAP) programme launched on 2 October 2021?
x: CLAP was launched on 2 October 2021 under the name Jagananna Swachha Sankalpam. Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra is a later state drive launched in January 2025.

s: APPCB has permitted how many cement industries to co-process incinerable, plastic and municipal waste?
x: APPCB permitted 12 cement industries to co-process incinerable, plastic and municipal waste.

s: Which pair of Andhra Pradesh cities is associated with WtE plants?
x: The cited Andhra Pradesh WtE plants are located at Guntur and Visakhapatnam.

s: In Swachh Survekshan 2022, which Andhra Pradesh city was named 'Top Impact Creator' (million-plus)?
x: Visakhapatnam was 'Top Impact Creator'; Tirupati came first in 'Safai Mitra Surakshit Shehar' (APPSC-G1 2022).

s: In August 2021, Andhra Pradesh became the first State with more than one of which of the following?
x: In Aug 2021 AP became the first State with more than one Water Plus city (three).

s: Under CLAP, households were given a three-bin set of which colours?
x: CLAP gave 40 lakh households a green, blue and red 3-bin set.

s: Which programme, launched in January 2025, is the successor of CLAP?
x: Swarna Andhra-Swachh Andhra (Jan 2025) succeeded CLAP (Jagananna Swachha Sankalpam).

s: From which date was Andhra Pradesh's ban on flexi banners deferred to take effect?
x: The flexi-banner ban was announced in Aug 2022 (G.O. Ms. No. 65) and deferred to 26 January 2023.

s: What is the role of the Swachha Andhra Corporation (SAC) in Andhra Pradesh?
o: State agency for urban sanitation under SBM-U 2.0
x: SAC is the state agency running urban sanitation under SBM-U 2.0; APEMC tracks hazardous-waste vehicles by GPS.

s: Under the CLAP programme, rural door-to-door garbage collection in Andhra Pradesh rose from 22% in November 2021 to what level by January 2022?
x: Under CLAP, rural door collection rose from 22% (Nov 2021) to 61.50% (Jan 2022).

s: Which Andhra Pradesh city came first in the 'Safai Mitra Surakshit Shehar' category in Swachh Survekshan 2022?
x: In Swachh Survekshan 2022 Tirupati came first in 'Safai Mitra Surakshit Shehar'; Visakhapatnam was 'Top Impact Creator'.

s: At which place is the Ongole legacy dumpsite being biomined, with the RDF sent to cement plants?
x: Ongole's legacy waste at Guthikondavaripalem is biomined and the RDF goes to cement plants.

s: What is the full form of REDD+?
x: REDD+ is Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation; India takes part and forest conservation can earn tradable credits.

s: Which terrestrial ecosystem stores more carbon per hectare than any other terrestrial ecosystem?
x: Tropical peatlands store more carbon per hectare than any other terrestrial ecosystem.

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the five IPCC carbon pools?
x: The five pools are above-ground biomass, below-ground biomass, dead wood, litter and soil organic carbon. Atmospheric oxygen is not one of them.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Mangroves are blue-carbon ecosystems. Automobiles burn petrol and diesel, thermal power plants burn coal, and Bhutan is a carbon-negative country.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mangroves are blue-carbon ecosystems.
2. Seagrass is part of blue-carbon ecosystems.
3. Salt marshes are blue-carbon ecosystems.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: All three are blue-carbon ecosystems: mangroves, seagrass and salt marshes store carbon in coastal waters.

s: As per ISFR 2023, what is India's approximate forest carbon stock?
x: ISFR 2023 put forest carbon stock at 7,285.5 Mt, up 81.5 Mt over 2021.

s: Which country is described as carbon-negative?
x: Bhutan is carbon-negative; net zero means emissions balanced by removals.

s: Which agencies run the UN-REDD programme, started in 2008?
x: UN-REDD (2008) is run by UNDP, FAO and UNEP.

s:
Consider the following statements about carbon sinks:
1. Forests, soil and oceans are natural carbon sinks.
2. Chlor-alkali plants are natural carbon sinks.
3. Carbon fertilisation accounts for about 70% of Earth's recent greening.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Forests, soil and oceans are natural sinks and CO2 fertilisation explains ~70% of recent greening; chlor-alkali plants are not sinks.

s: What is increased plant growth caused by higher atmospheric CO2 raising the rate of photosynthesis called?
x: Carbon fertilisation is faster plant growth driven by extra CO2 speeding up photosynthesis.

s: India's first community-based REDD+ project, the Khasi Hills project, is in which State?
x: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ Project in East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya, is India's first community REDD+ project (Plan Vivo).

s: What is the carbon stored by oceans and coastal ecosystems called?
x: Blue carbon is carbon stored by oceans and coastal ecosystems; geological storage uses coal seams, depleted reservoirs and saline formations.

s: Under which programme is the National Carbon Project implemented?
o: National Action Plan on Climate Change
x: The National Carbon Project is under the ISRO Geosphere-Biosphere Programme and assesses carbon pools, fluxes and net carbon balance of India's terrestrial biomes.

s: Which pair of satellites is correctly associated with CO2 observation?
x: NASA's OCO-2 and Japan's GOSAT are CO2-observing satellites.

s: What is the main goal of the National Carbon Project under the ISRO Geosphere-Biosphere Programme?
o: Assessing carbon pools, fluxes and net carbon balance of India's terrestrial biomes
Developing space technology for carbon sequestration
Fixing the price of carbon credits
x: The National Carbon Project assesses carbon pools, fluxes and net carbon balance of India's land biomes using remote sensing.

s: Which of the following is NOT a goal of the National Carbon Project?
o: Developing space technology for carbon sequestration
x: The project studies carbon pools, fluxes and balance with remote-sensing databases; it does not develop space technology for sequestration.

s: NET Power's Allam-Fetvedt cycle plant burns natural gas in oxygen. What does it use as the working fluid?
x: The La Porte, Texas plant burns gas in oxygen with supercritical CO2 as the working fluid and captures nearly all its CO2.

s: What is the process of capturing CO2 from industrial processes and storing it so that it does not enter the atmosphere called?
x: This is carbon sequestration (APPSC-GS 2024 key). Carbon leakage is emissions moving abroad; offsetting uses credits to balance emissions.

s: Which technology combines bioenergy with carbon capture and storage to give net-negative emissions?
x: BECCS (Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage) gives net-negative emissions.

s: Which carbon-removal method pulls CO2 straight from ambient air?
x: Direct Air Capture pulls CO2 from ambient air; enhanced rock weathering spreads crushed silicate rock on land.

s: What does the DST's cement-sector initiative on carbon capture and utilisation consist of?
o: three CCU testbeds forming a regional demonstration network
seven DAC testbeds for urban transport
five CCU testbeds forming a first-of-its-kind research cluster
five CCS testbeds located only in coal mines
x: DST has established five Carbon Capture and Utilisation testbeds in the cement sector as a first-of-its-kind research cluster.

s: Which statement correctly distinguishes CCS from CCUS?
o: CCS uses CO2, while CCUS only stores it
Both only release CO2 to the air
CCS removes CO2 from ambient air
CCS only stores captured CO2, while CCUS uses or stores it
x: CCS = capture, transport and storage only; CCUS = capture, then use or store.

s: What is spreading crushed basalt on farmland to bind CO2 as carbonate called?
x: Enhanced rock weathering uses crushed silicate rock like basalt; ocean alkalinity enhancement adds lime to seawater.

s: What is adding lime or alkaline minerals to seawater to remove CO2 known as?
x: Ocean alkalinity enhancement adds lime or alkaline minerals to seawater.

s: How many steps does the CCS process involve?
o: Four – capture, use, transport and release
x: CCS has three steps: capture at a stationary point source, transport and storage.

s: Which of the following is NOT a geological storage site for captured CO2?
x: Geological storage uses coal seams, depleted oil and gas reservoirs and deep saline formations; mangroves are blue-carbon sinks, not geological storage.

s: Gold Standard, a voluntary carbon standard, was founded by which organisation?
x: Gold Standard was founded by WWF, the World Wide Fund for Nature.

s: What does the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) under the Kyoto Protocol issue?
x: The CDM issues Certified Emission Reductions (CERs); the VCS is run by Verra. One carbon credit equals one tonne CO2e.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS)?
o: It is India's first mandatory compliance carbon market.
It was notified under Section 14AA of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
It is administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power.
x: Section 14AA belongs to the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, not the Environment (Protection) Act.

s: Under which scheme were emission-intensity targets for aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali and pulp and paper notified in October 2025?
x: These sectoral emission-intensity targets were notified under India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS).

s: Which of the following correctly characterises the Budget 2026–27 carbon credit programme?
o: It follows the DST roadmap and is industrial in orientation, rather than being a farmer-only scheme.
It is a panchayat-level programme focused only on blue carbon.
It follows the Kyoto Protocol and is administered exclusively by WWF.
It is a voluntary scheme restricted to 282 agricultural entities.
x: The programme follows the DST roadmap and concerns industrial carbon credits; it is not a farmer-only scheme.

s: What does one carbon credit represent?
x: One carbon credit equals one tonne of CO2e avoided or removed.

s: Which organisation runs the Verified Carbon Standard (VCS)?
x: VCS is run by Verra; Gold Standard was founded by WWF.

s: Which body runs India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme?
x: The CCTS is run by BEE and trades Indian Carbon Credits; it is India's first mandatory compliance market.

s: India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme was notified under which provision?
x: CCTS (June 2023) was notified under Sec. 14AA of the Energy Conservation Act 2001, not the EP Act.

s: How are the prices of carbon credits set?
x: Carbon credit prices are set by supply and demand in the market, not fixed by UNEP or any international body.

s: Which Ministry launched the Net Zero Portal for voluntary net-zero disclosure in September 2026?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
x: The Net Zero Portal (MoEFCC, September 2026) is for voluntary net-zero disclosure.

s: Under which Article of the EU CBAM Regulation can a carbon price already paid, such as under India's CCTS, be deducted?
x: Article 9 allows deduction of a carbon price already paid; CBAM revenue stays in Europe.

s: Which pair correctly identifies the first country to propose and the first country to actually levy a livestock carbon tax?
x: New Zealand was the first country to propose a tax on agricultural emissions, while Denmark is to become the first to actually levy a livestock carbon tax from 2030.

s: On which date did the definitive phase of the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) start?
x: CBAM had a transitional phase from 2023 and its definitive phase began on 1 January 2026; certificates are priced on the EU ETS.

s: On which date does the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) start?
x: The UK CBAM starts on 1 January 2027; the EU CBAM's definitive phase began on 1 January 2026.

s: What does the EU CBAM aim to prevent?
x: CBAM levies carbon on imports to stop carbon leakage, i.e. emissions moving abroad.

s: From which year will Denmark levy its livestock carbon tax?
x: New Zealand proposed a livestock tax first; Denmark is the first to levy one, from 2030.

s: Which of the following is NOT covered by the EU CBAM?
x: CBAM covers iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity; textiles are not listed.

s: Which footprint measures freshwater use as blue, green and grey water?
x: The water footprint counts freshwater use as blue, green and grey water; the ecological footprint is the land and water needed to support consumption and absorb waste.

s: A company's diesel generator emits greenhouse gases, its purchased electricity causes indirect emissions, and emissions occur in the manufacture and transport of its purchased inputs. How are these classified, respectively?
x: Direct emissions from owned sources are Scope 1, emissions from purchased electricity or heat are Scope 2, and the remaining value-chain emissions are Scope 3.

s: What does the carbon footprint measure?
o: Total greenhouse gases produced, directly and indirectly, to support human activities
Land and water area needed to produce what we consume and absorb our waste
Freshwater used as blue, green and grey water
Carbon stored in forests and soils
x: Carbon footprint is the total greenhouse gases (in tonnes CO2e a year) produced directly and indirectly by human activities.

s: What does the ecological footprint measure?
o: Freshwater used as blue, green and grey water
Land and water area needed to produce what we consume and absorb our waste
Total greenhouse gases produced by human activities
Carbon stored in oceans and coastal ecosystems
x: Ecological footprint is the land and water needed to produce what we consume and to absorb our waste.

s: Palli village in Samba district was declared India’s first carbon-neutral panchayat in which year?
x: Palli in Samba, Jammu and Kashmir, was declared India’s first carbon-neutral panchayat in 2022.

s: Which Union Territory's carbon-neutral effort includes solar water lifting, passive solar buildings, geothermal heating and electric vehicles?
x: These measures are part of Ladakh's effort to become a carbon-neutral Union Territory.

s: Which is India's first Level 5 net-zero airport (2024)?
x: Delhi airport became India's first Level 5 net-zero airport in 2024; Cochin is the world's first fully solar-powered airport.

s: Which is the world's first fully solar-powered airport (2015)?
x: Cochin airport became the world's first fully solar-powered airport in 2015.

s: Maruti Suzuki's Gujarat rail siding is the world's first modal-shift project registered with:
x: It is the world's first modal-shift project under Verra's VCS.

s: Which airport became the first carbon-neutral airport in the Asia-Pacific region in 2016?
x: Delhi airport was the first carbon-neutral airport in Asia-Pacific (2016) and India's first Level 5 net-zero airport (2024).

s: NITI Aayog's decarbonisation roadmaps for the cement, aluminium and MSME sectors rely on which combination of measures?
o: Round-the-clock renewable-energy power, nuclear power and CCUS
Hydropower, biofuels and ocean alkalinity enhancement only
Natural gas, nuclear disarmament and direct air capture only
Coal expansion, diesel generation and afforestation only
x: The roadmaps rely on renewable energy available round the clock, nuclear power and carbon capture, utilisation and storage.

s: From FY 2025-26, coal-based power plants must co-fire what share of biomass?
x: The co-firing requirement is 5% in FY 2024-25 and 7% from FY 2025-26, monitored by the SAMARTH mission.

s: In which State is the Gevra coal mine, listed among India's 'carbon bombs', located?
x: Gevra is in Chhattisgarh and Rajmahal in Jharkhand; a carbon bomb is a fossil project that could emit over 1 Gt CO2 in its lifetime.

s: India's 2035 NDC targets what cut in emission intensity compared with 2005?
x: The 2035 NDC targets a 47% cut in emission intensity vs 2005 and 60% non-fossil power capacity.

s: As per the Global Carbon Budget 2025, what is India's rank among fossil-CO2 emitting countries?
x: China (~31.8%) leads, then the USA (~12.7%), then India (~8.3%, 3rd).

s: What is India's approximate per capita CO2 emission?
o: 2 tonnes, the lowest in the G20
x: India emits about 2 t CO2 per capita against a world average of ~4.7 t, the lowest in the G20.

s: The cement sector accounts for about what share of India's GHG emissions?
x: Cement is about 6%, aluminium about 2.8% and waste 2.56% (2020, BUR-4).

s: A 'carbon bomb' is a fossil-fuel project that could emit more than how much CO2 in its lifetime?
x: Carbon bombs are projects that could emit over 1 Gt CO2; India's include Gevra and Rajmahal coal mines.

s: India's 2035 NDC targets what share of non-fossil power capacity?
x: The 2035 NDC targets 60% non-fossil power capacity and a 47% emission-intensity cut over 2005.

s: Which country is the largest emitter of fossil CO2 as per the Global Carbon Budget 2025?
x: China (about 31.8%) leads, followed by the USA (about 12.7%) and India (about 8.3%).

s: In which State is the Rajmahal coal mine, listed among India's 'carbon bombs', located?
x: India's carbon bombs include Gevra (Chhattisgarh) and Rajmahal (Jharkhand) coal mines.

s: Which mission monitors biomass co-firing in coal-based thermal power plants?
x: The SAMARTH mission watches biomass co-firing, which rises from 5% (FY 2024-25) to 7% (FY 2025-26).

s: Which is the only Blue Flag beach of Andhra Pradesh, whose status was restored in March 2025?
x: Rushikonda in Visakhapatnam is AP's only Blue Flag beach (2020), restored in March 2025.

s: On what basis does the APPCB allot industrial inspections through its computerised system?
x: APPCB uses computerised, risk-based inspection allocation and has SOPs for effluents, marine outfalls and hazardous waste.

s: How did the Andhra Pradesh government decide to check industrial pollution in September 2019?
o: Imposing and collecting a green tax from industrial houses
Banning all industries near water bodies
Launching the Blue Flag programme for beaches
x: In September 2019 AP decided to impose and collect a green tax from industrial houses (PYQ). Siting near water bodies is handled by APPCB guidelines, not a blanket ban; APPCB (est. 1976) continues; Blue Flag is an FEE eco-label.

s: With which of the following is BRAP associated in Andhra Pradesh's environmental initiatives?
x: BRAP is associated with a single-window system, while APPCB is associated with siting guidelines.

s: In which year did Andhra Pradesh impose a green tax on industrial houses to check pollution?
x: AP imposed the green tax on industrial houses in September 2019.

s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board (APPCB) established?
x: APPCB was established in 1976.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ecomark Rules, 2024 – Run alongside the 1991 Ecomark scheme
Ecomark Rules, 2024 – Prevent misleading green claims
1991 Ecomark scheme – Still in force today
x: The Ecomark Rules notified in September 2024 aim to stop misleading green claims; they replaced the 1991 scheme.

s: What is PRAMAAN associated with?
o: Certification of electric vehicle charging stations
Voluntary third-party certification for sustainable forestry and agroforestry
Certification of indoor air quality in hospitals
x: PRAMAAN is a voluntary third-party forest and wood certification initiative for sustainable forestry and agroforestry.

s: How many Indian beaches were recommended for Blue Flag certification in 2020?
x: Eight Indian beaches were recommended for Blue Flag certification in 2020.

s: Which body awards the 'Blue Flag' eco-label for beaches?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
International Union for Conservation of Nature
x: Blue Flag is an international beach eco-label of the Foundation for Environmental Education (FEE), Denmark. UNEP, MoEFCC and IUCN do not award it; MoEFCC ran Ecomark (1991).

s: Which body administers the Green Credit Programme?
x: ICFRE is the administrator of the Green Credit Programme.

s: Which activity was the first to become operational under the Green Credit Programme?
x: Of the eight activities, tree plantation became operational first.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Green Credit Programme:
1. Its rules were notified in October 2023.
2. It covers eight activities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: rules were notified in October 2023 and the programme lists eight activities.

s: Which of the following product categories is covered under the Ecomark scheme?
x: Ecomark covers products such as soaps, detergents, paper, plastics, cosmetics and aerosols, but not drugs and antibiotics.

s: In which year was the Ecomark scheme launched by the Government of India?
x: Ecomark was launched in 1991; the Ecomark Rules of 2024 replaced that scheme.

s: From which date did BS-VI emission norms come into force in India?
x: BS-VI norms apply from 1 April 2020.

s: India's National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) prescribe standards for how many pollutants?
x: NAAQS prescribe standards for 12 pollutants.

s: The Jan Vishwas reforms mark a shift in regulatory approach from what to what?
o: Trust-based regulation to manual command-and-control regulation
Technology-enabled regulation to prohibition of digital systems
Command-and-control regulation to trust-based, technology-enabled regulation
Judicial regulation to complete self-regulation without technology
x: The reforms are described as moving regulation from a command-and-control model to trust-based, technology-enabled regulation.

s: In which year was the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, which replaced jail with monetary penalties for minor offences under the Air Act and EP Act, passed?
x: The Jan Vishwas Act was passed in 2023; the Water Act was amended likewise in 2024.

s: Under the 2026 Rules, in what ratio is the Environmental (Protection) Fund shared between States/UTs and the Centre?
x: The Fund (Section 16, EP Act; audited by the CAG) is shared 75% States/UTs and 25% Centre.

s: In August 2025, under which provisions did the Supreme Court uphold the power of Pollution Control Boards to impose environmental compensation?
o: Section 33A of the Water Act and Section 31A of the Air Act
Section 16 of the Environment (Protection) Act alone
Section 33A of the Air Act and Section 31A of the Water Act
x: The Supreme Court upheld PCB power under Section 33A of the Water Act and Section 31A of the Air Act.

s: Which statement correctly describes the revised industrial categories?
o: The mandatory 33% green belt was retained without any change.
All industries were placed in one category based only on location.
A new Blue category was introduced, and the mandatory 33% green belt was replaced by pollution-potential norms.
The Blue category was abolished, and a mandatory 50% green belt was introduced.
x: The revised categories introduced a new Blue category, illustrated by compressed biogas, and replaced the mandatory 33% green belt requirement with pollution-potential norms.

s: Who audits the Environmental (Protection) Fund under the 2026 Rules?
x: Penalties go to the Fund under Section 16 of the EP Act, and the Fund is audited by the CAG.

s: From January 2026, for how long is a Consent to Operate (CTO) for industries valid?
x: Since January 2026 the Consent to Operate remains valid till cancelled.

s: In which year was the Water Act amended to decriminalise minor offences, replacing jail with penalties?
x: After the Jan Vishwas Act 2023 (Air Act, EP Act), the Water Act was amended in 2024 likewise.

s: Under the Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026, penalties go to the Fund under which section of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
x: Penalties go to the Fund under Section 16 of the EPA, shared 75:25 between States/UTs and the Centre.

s: What is PARIVESH 3.0 mainly designed as?
o: single-window portal for clearances and compliance monitoring
grant scheme for strengthening Pollution Control Boards
programme for replacing BS-IV vehicles with BS-VI vehicles
mobile application for publishing air-quality readings
x: PARIVESH 3.0 functions as a single-window portal for environmental clearances and compliance monitoring.

s: Whom are Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs) meant to serve?
x: CETPs serve clusters of small industries; SAAP (1992) gives grants to strengthen Pollution Control Boards.

s: Online continuous emission monitoring is compulsory for highly polluting industries of how many categories?
x: CPCB requires online continuous monitoring for the 17 categories of highly polluting industries.

s: For what does the SAAP scheme of 1992 give grants?
x: SAAP (1992) gives grants to strengthen Pollution Control Boards.

s: PM E-DRIVE (2024) is the successor to which scheme for electric mobility?
x: PM E-DRIVE (2024) gives EV and charging incentives, succeeding FAME; PM-KUSUM is for farm solar pumps.

s: For what does the UNEP-CCAC 'Hidden Assets' assessment identify PMUY as a model programme?
x: The assessment cites PMUY as a model clean-cooking programme and identifies clean cooking and heating as South Asia’s leading solution towards 2035.

s: What does PM-KUSUM (2019) mainly support?
o: Solar pumps and solar plants for farms
x: PM-KUSUM funds farm solar pumps and solar plants; rooftop solar for homes is PM Surya Ghar.

s: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana gives up to how many units of free electricity a month?
x: PM Surya Ghar (Feb 2024) provides rooftop solar to 1 crore homes with up to 300 free units a month.

s: Which of the following pairs (scheme – launch) is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana – 2019
x: PM Surya Ghar was launched in February 2024; 2019 is the launch year of PM-KUSUM.

s: What is the main objective of the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (2016)?
o: Free LPG connections to poor households to cut indoor smoke
x: PM Ujjwala Yojana gives free LPG to poor households, reducing indoor smoke from cooking.

s: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana aims to provide rooftop solar to how many homes?
x: PM Surya Ghar (Feb 2024) aims at rooftop solar for 1 crore homes with up to 300 free units a month.

s: By what other name is Portland limestone cement known?
x: Portland limestone cement is green cement, an example of green technology in the cement industry.

s: How is incineration of waste classified?
o: A conventional method of waste treatment
x: Incineration is a conventional waste-treatment method and is not classified as an alternative pollution-control approach in this context.

s: From which of the following does carbon capture and storage (CCS) capture CO2?
o: Point sources such as cement plants
x: CCS captures CO2 from point sources such as cement plants; it remains largely at the research stage.

s: How does bioremediation compare with conventional pollution-control methods?
x: Bioremediation is eco-friendly and cost-effective but slower, and its results vary with local conditions.

s: Which body released India's R&D Roadmap for Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage in December 2025?
x: The Department of Science and Technology (DST) released the CCUS R&D Roadmap in December 2025.

s: Under India's CCUS R&D Roadmap, for which period is commercial-scale deployment planned?
x: The roadmap runs pilots 2025–30, industrial integration 2030–35 and commercial scale 2035–45.

s: The NTPC Vindhyachal CCUS pilot captures about how much CO2 a day?
x: The NTPC Vindhyachal pilot captures about 20 tonnes of CO2 a day.

s:
Consider the following statements about carbon capture in India:
1. DST approved five CCUS test beds in May 2025.
2. Budget 2026 proposed ₹20,000 crore for CCUS.
3. CCS for cement plants has reached commercial scale.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; CCS for cement is still largely at the research stage.
